Across three seeds, AR GAR-ours rises from 0.064 to $0.401\pm0.047$ (seeds: 0.347 / 0.423 / 0.433; per-seed details in Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-perseed}), compressing the gap from 7.8$\times$ to ${\sim}$1.3$\times$ (per-seed gaps: 1.45$\times$, 1.17$\times$, 1.15$\times$; TF GAR $0.498\pm0.004$) with no PPL cost ($1.441\pm0.001$; Figure~\ref{fig:ss-gap}). Steering on SS models is remarkably stable ($\beta$\,=\,5: $0.717\pm0.001$): the training-time seed variance (std\,=\,0.047 at $\beta$\,=\,0) is nearly eliminated (Figure~\ref{fig:ss-multiseed}), suggesting $\beta$-steering converges to a seed-independent attention equilibrium. The improvement generalizes across GAR definitions: SS raises mid-turn GAR above 0.36 under all four alternative token-position variants (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-gar-robust}), while ThreadGate only improves last-token GAR (0.325 vs.\ all-token 0.025): SS builds a broad goal-attention pattern, not position-specific overfitting. GAR-Dongre also rises substantially under SS ($N$\,=\,5 pilot; see Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-n5}), the only intervention that moves both metrics. The benefit diminishes in longer dialogues (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-n5}), consistent with exposure bias compounding over turns.

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

A five-way controlled comparison on ThreadGate, per-layer content-and-turn-conditioned gates with an auxiliary GAR loss, reveals that training succeeds (TF GAR\,=\,0.50) but autoregressive GAR collapses 8--17$\times$ on Qwen-2.5-7B (27$\times$ (median) on Llama-3.1-8B). Each ablation pair kills one hypothesis; the failure traces to exposure bias, classical in origin but with no prior multi-turn transformer characterization. Steering ($\beta$\,=\,5) recovers GAR to 0.727, confirming attention misallocation as the proximal cause. Scheduled sampling compresses the gap from 8$\times$ to ${\sim}$1.3$\times$ with no perplexity cost ($0.401\pm0.047$, three seeds), the first transfer of time-scheduled sampling to auxiliary attention objectives in multi-turn transformers.
